disorder-name.detail: First-episode schizophrenia spectrum disorder diagnosed with SCID-I (DSM-IV), comprising schizophrenia (n=57, 72%), schizophreniform disorder (n=18, 23%), and schizoaffective disorder (n=4, 5%). The paper labels this clinical cohort as 'SCZ' but explicitly frames the study as first-episode psychosis (FEP) in both the title and methods. Normative models were applied at 3 timepoints: baseline (N=79), 12-month follow-up (N=67), and 10-year follow-up (N=23).
disorder-name.supporting_text: "patients with a first-episode schizophrenia spectrum diagnosis (SCZ) were consecutively recruited from the catchment-area-based inpatient and outpatient services at Oslo University Hospital" and "schizophrenia (n=57, 72% of the final, quality-checked longitudinal sample), schizophreniform disorders (n=18, 23%), and schizoaffective (n=4, 5%)"

dataset-of-origin.detail: The Thematically Organized Psychosis (TOP) study at the University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital. Longitudinal first-episode sub-study with recruitment from October 27, 2004 to October 17, 2012. Three MRI scanners were used: 1.5T Siemens Sonata (TOP15), 3T GE Signa HDxt (TOP3T), and 3T GE Discovery 750 (TOP3TGE).
dataset-of-origin.supporting_text: "All participants were recruited to a specific first-episode sub-study of the TOP study at the University of Oslo and Oslo University Hospital from October 27, 2004, to October 17, 2012."

sex.detail: Baseline SCZ cohort (N=79). Female ratio 41.7% from Table 1. Female N estimated as round(79 × 0.417) = 33 (estimated from percentage); male N = 79 − 33 = 46 (estimated by subtraction). Percentages recalculated from estimated counts: female 33/79 = 41.8%, male 46/79 = 58.2%.
